PART I

ITEM 1.  BUSINESS

Bluewater Energy Corporation (“Bluewater”) is an independent oil and natural gas company engaged in the exploration, development and production of crude oil and natural gas in the Permian Basin and the Gulf of Mexico. At December 31, 2015, our estimated proved reserves were 412 million barrels of oil equivalent.

Our strategy is to grow production through disciplined development drilling while maintaining a strong balance sheet. Our operations are discussed further under Item 7, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis.”

1

ITEM 1A.  RISK FACTORS

Oil and natural gas prices are volatile, and a sustained decline in prices could adversely affect our financial condition.

Our revenues, profitability and future growth depend substantially on prevailing prices for oil and natural gas. During 2015, the price of West Texas Intermediate crude oil fell below $35 per barrel, the lowest level since 2009. A continued period of low prices would reduce our cash flows and borrowing capacity and could require us to record impairments of our oil and gas properties.

Our hedging activities may limit the benefit of price increases and expose us to counterparty risk.

We enter into derivative contracts to reduce exposure to commodity price volatility. These contracts may prevent us from realizing the benefit of price increases and expose us to the risk that a counterparty fails to perform.

5

Offshore operations involve special risks that could affect our operations adversely.

Offshore operations are subject to hurricanes, loop currents and other adverse weather conditions. A well blowout or oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico could result in significant liabilities and regulatory penalties.

ITEM 3.  LEGAL PROCEEDINGS

In June 2015, the State of Louisiana filed suit against Bluewater and other operators alleging damage to coastal wetlands. We intend to vigorously defend this action.

8

PART II

ITEM 7.  MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Overview

Our 2015 results were significantly affected by the decline in commodity prices. Revenues decreased 46% to $2.1 billion and we recorded impairments of $1.4 billion related to our Gulf of Mexico properties.

Results of Operations

Oil production averaged 142 thousand barrels per day, an increase of 8% from 2014 driven by Permian Basin development. Lease operating expense per barrel decreased 12% due to cost reduction initiatives and lower service costs.

ITEM 7A.  QUANTITATIVE AND QUALITATIVE DISCLOSURES ABOUT MARKET RISK

Our primary market risk is commodity price volatility. A 10% decline in oil prices would have reduced 2015 revenues by approximately $180 million, before the effect of derivatives.
